questions.question: A person working on a disabled vehicle on the shoulder of a road:

options.text: Will likely pay attention to traffic on the road.
May be focused on the repair and not notice traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: May be focused on the repair and not notice traffic.
questions.explanation: Be careful when driving near people working on disabled vehicles. They are focused on their repair work and may not notice traffic or other dangers on the road.

questions.question: During a trip, which shut-off valves should be open?

options.text: All shut-off valves should be open.
The rear shut-off valves should be open.
All shut-off valves should be open, except the rear shut-off valves.
No shut-off valves should be open.

questions.correctAnswerText: All shut-off valves should be open, except the rear shut-off valves.
questions.explanation: When starting a trip, open all shut-off valves except the rear ones. This lets air reach the brakes on all trailers and prevents air from escaping the back of the vehicle.

questions.question: When coupling a trailer:

options.text: Any glad hand can be connected to any other glad hand.
It is best to leave one glad hand unattached.
Only one set of glad hands should be connected.

questions.explanation: Connect only matching glad hands. They are often color-coded to help drivers avoid mistakes. Blue is usually for service lines and red is usually for emergency lines.

questions.question: A pre-trip vehicle inspection:

options.text: Is not required if you use the vehicle regularly.
Is not required for trips under 100 miles.
Can only be done by a mechanic.

questions.explanation: State and federal law require drivers to inspect their vehicles before starting to drive.

questions.question: Hazardous materials may be transported:

options.text: By any driver with a CDL.
By any driver if the hazardous materials weigh less than 50 pounds.
By any driver in a rural area.
By a driver with a CDL and HazMat endorsement.

questions.correctAnswerText: By a driver with a CDL and HazMat endorsement.
questions.explanation: You need a CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement to drive any vehicle used to transport hazardous materials.

questions.question: HazMat endorsement holders must be fingerprinted:

options.text: Every time the endorsement is renewed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Every time the endorsement is renewed.
questions.explanation: When you apply for or renew a HazMat endorsement, you must complete a Federal Security Threat Assessment, which includes being fingerprinted.

questions.question: A loss of air pressure in the emergency line will cause:

options.text: The tractor protection valve to open.
The rear trailer to detach from the combination.

questions.explanation: The emergency air line controls the emergency brakes on a combination vehicle. If air pressure is lost in the emergency line, the emergency trailer brakes will activate.

questions.question: Emergency response information from the shipper must include:

options.text: Any risks of fire or explosion.
How many people should respond in an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Any risks of fire or explosion.
questions.explanation: Emergency response information must include basic descriptions and technical names of materials, health hazards, fire or explosion risks, safety steps for accidents, fire handling methods, spill or leak handling methods, and first aid measures.

questions.question: If you are driving slowly and could slow down other vehicles, you should:

options.text: Wave an arm out of your window.

questions.explanation: If you must drive slowly, use your emergency flashers to warn other drivers. Check your local laws to make sure emergency flashers are allowed.

questions.question: What can change the height of a vehicle?
questions.explanation: A heavy load makes a vehicle sit lower than when it is empty. A vehicle is taller when it carries a light load than when it carries a heavy load. If your vehicle fits under an overpass when fully loaded, it may not fit when empty.

questions.question: Shaded areas of the road:

options.text: Usually have no moisture, so they cannot freeze.
Stay slippery after ice melts on other parts of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay slippery after ice melts on other parts of the road.
questions.explanation: Shaded areas get less sunlight and stay cooler longer than other road areas. These spots can remain icy and slippery even after ice has melted elsewhere.

questions.question: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS):

options.text: Makes a loud squeaking noise when you use it.
Helps you keep control while braking.

questions.correctAnswerText: Helps you keep control while braking.
questions.explanation: ABS helps you stay in control when braking. It does not necessarily change how far your vehicle travels before it stops.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Move quickly before another vehicle gets into the lane you want.
Move slowly in case another vehicle is already in the lane you want.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move slowly in case another vehicle is already in the lane you want.
questions.explanation: Always change lanes slowly and smoothly. This gives other drivers time to move or honk a warning if you did not see them. Always signal before changing lanes.

questions.question: How many hours of sleep does an adult need each day to stay alert?
questions.explanation: Getting enough rest is important for safe driving. Most adults need eight to nine hours of sleep each night to stay alert.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a shipping paper?
questions.explanation: Shipping papers describe the hazardous materials being transported. Shipping orders, bills of lading, and manifests are all shipping papers. Directions are not.

questions.question: What is the leading cause of death and injury in work zones?
questions.explanation: Speeding is the main cause of deaths and injuries in work zones. Drive carefully when near road workers.

questions.question: After the engine starts, warning lights and buzzers should:

options.text: Turn off once the vehicle starts moving.

questions.explanation: Warning lights and buzzers should turn off right away when the engine starts. This includes the charging circuit warning light, oil light, coolant light, and Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) light.

questions.question: Mirror adjustment can only be checked properly when:

options.text: There is no trailer attached to the tractor.
The vehicle is on a slight incline.
The vehicle is on a slight decline.

questions.explanation: When a trailer is attached to a tractor, you can only check mirror adjustment accurately if the trailer is straight.

questions.question: Which of these is most likely to cause hydroplaning?
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning is most likely on wet roads when tire pressure is low or tread is worn. Hydroplaning can happen at speeds as low as 30 mph if there is enough water on the road.

questions.question: Hazardous materials laws are set by:
questions.explanation: Because hazardous materials are risky, federal, state, and local governments all have rules for how they must be transported.

questions.question: If you need to stop quickly while carrying liquids, what is a safe option?
questions.explanation: Tank vehicles carrying liquids are less stable than other vehicles. They can roll over or skid if not operated safely. If you need to stop quickly to avoid an accident, use controlled braking or stab braking.

questions.question: Is rough acceleration a good driving practice?

options.text: Yes, it is good at slow speeds.
Yes, it is good at all speeds.
No, it can damage the vehicle.
No, it can confuse other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, it can damage the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Speed up smoothly and gradually. Rough acceleration can cause the vehicle to jerk and may damage it.

questions.question: What should you do when loading or unloading explosive materials?

options.text: Use sharp tools to open packages.

questions.explanation: Always turn off the engine before loading or unloading explosives. Never drop, throw, or roll packages containing explosives.

questions.question: When backing a trailer, which way should you turn the steering wheel?

options.text: Turn the top of the steering wheel toward where you want the trailer to go.
Turn the top of the steering wheel away from where you want the trailer to go.
It depends on where you are backing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the top of the steering wheel away from where you want the trailer to go.
questions.explanation: When backing with a trailer, turn the steering wheel away from where you want to go. Once the trailer starts turning, switch the steering wheel direction to follow the trailer.

questions.question: How can you prevent a manual transmission vehicle from rolling backward when starting?

options.text: Partly engage the clutch before releasing the brake pedal.
Put the vehicle in reverse before moving forward.
Fully engage the clutch before releasing the brake pedal.
Put the vehicle in neutral before moving forward.

questions.correctAnswerText: Partly engage the clutch before releasing the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: To prevent rolling backward when starting, partly engage the clutch before releasing the brake. Use the parking brake when needed to prevent rolling back.

questions.question: What is the service air line attached to?
questions.explanation: The service air line carries air controlled by the foot brake or trailer hand brake. It connects to relay valves, which allow the trailer brakes to be applied quickly.

questions.question: Which is not a sign of drowsiness?
questions.explanation: Drowsy driving is dangerous and must be avoided. Signs of drowsiness include frequent blinking, eyes closing or losing focus, frequent yawning, and drifting between lanes.

questions.question: Which is not a correct turn signal rule?

options.text: Keep the signal on during the turn.
Turn off the signal after the turn is complete.
Only signal if another vehicle is nearby.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only signal if another vehicle is nearby.
questions.explanation: Always signal before turning or changing lanes. Start signaling well before the movement and keep it on during the turn. Turn off the signal after your turn or lane change is complete.

questions.question: How must hazardous material containers be prepared for transport?

options.text: Secured to prevent movement during transport.
Limited to a maximum height of four feet.

questions.correctAnswerText: Secured to prevent movement during transport.
questions.explanation: Hazardous material containers must be secured so they will not fall, slide, or bounce during transport.

questions.question: What can help reduce stress while driving?
questions.explanation: Stress while driving can lead to aggressive driving, which is dangerous. Calming music can help you relax and reduce stress while driving.
